contentEn:
Most homes in Vancouver's Kerrisdale, Dunbar, and Riley Park neighbourhoods were wired with 60-amp electrical services when they were built. A 60-amp panel cannot safely power a modern kitchen with induction cooktops, heat pump water heaters, and EV chargers running simultaneously. Reno Stars upgrades these panels to 100 or 200 amps as part of whole-home renovations and major rewires.

When Does a Vancouver Home Need a Panel Upgrade?

A panel upgrade is triggered when the existing service cannot handle the projected load. The Canadian Electrical Code requires a load calculation before any new large appliance is added. If the sum of your existing circuits plus a new induction range (typically 40–60 amps) exceeds the panel rating, an upgrade is required before the renovation can pass inspection.

Reno Stars includes a load calculation in every whole-home renovation estimate. This is not optional — BC Safety Authority requires it before issuing an electrical permit for service upgrades in Vancouver.

What the Upgrade Involves

The work follows a predictable sequence. First, the local utility (BC Hydro in Vancouver) disconnects the service drop. The old panel is removed and a new 100-amp or 200-amp breaker panel is installed. New branch circuits are run to each room, typically using 14 AWG wire for lighting and 12 AWG for general outlets. Kitchen ranges require a dedicated 40–60-amp 240-volt circuit.

Permit fees in Vancouver run approximately $200–$300 for the electrical permit, and BC Hydro may charge $300–$600 to upgrade the service drop depending on the distance from the transformer. Total material cost for a 100-amp panel upgrade is typically $1,500–$3,000, with labour adding $1,000–$2,500 depending on the age of the wiring.

Planning a kitchen, bathroom, whole-home or commercial renovation? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars.

Panel Upgrade Timeline in a Vancouver Renovation

A straightforward 100-amp panel replacement takes one to two days. If the renovation involves rewiring the entire home at the same time — as in a whole-house renovation — the electrical phase typically spans two to three weeks. The timeline breaks down as follows:

  • Load calculation and permit application: 3–7 business days (Vancouver inspection authority)
  • BC Hydro service disconnect and reconnect: coordinated booking, typically 1–2 weeks in advance
  • Panel replacement and initial circuits: 1–2 days
  • Final circuit trim and inspection: 1 day

Reno Stars coordinates directly with BC Hydro and the Vancouver inspection office so the homeowner does not manage any of these bookings. This avoids the most common delay: a homeowner waiting for a utility appointment they did not know they had to schedule.

2025 Canadian Electrical Code Changes Affecting Vancouver Renovations

The 2025 Canadian Electrical Code (CEC) introduced stricter requirements for arc-fault circuit interrupters (AFCIs) in residential bedrooms and kitchens, and expanded the requirement for surge protection in new panel installations. These changes apply to all permits applied for after January 1, 2025. Reno Stars specifications for new panel installs include a combination AFCI/breaker panel as standard, which satisfies the 2025 CEC requirement without a separate surge protection device.

Homes with fuse-style panels (the round glass fuses found in pre-1965 Vancouver houses) are not grandfathered under the 2025 code. Any renovation triggering an electrical permit must bring the panel up to current code, including arc-fault protection throughout.

How Much Does a Panel Upgrade Cost in Vancouver?

Based on Reno Stars project records for Vancouver-area renovations completed in 2025, a 100-amp panel upgrade during a whole-home renovation typically ranges from $2,500 to $5,500 total (materials, labour, permit, and utility coordination). A 200-amp upgrade, required for homes adding multiple EV chargers or a heat pump HVAC system, ranges from $4,000 to $8,000.

These figures are consistent with BC Hydro's published estimates for service upgrades in the Metro Vancouver area. Exact cost depends on the distance from the BC Hydro transformer and whether the existing conduit run can be reused.

Planning a kitchen, bathroom, whole-home or commercial renovation? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a 60-amp panel need to be upgraded for a kitchen renovation in Vancouver?

Most likely yes, if you are adding an induction cooktop, double oven, or electric tankless water heater. Vancouver building code requires a load calculation before these appliances can be connected. If the calculation shows the existing 60-amp service is insufficient, an upgrade to at least 100 amps is required before the renovation passes inspection.

How long does a panel upgrade take during a whole-home renovation?

A 100-amp panel replacement takes one to two days for the physical installation. Because BC Hydro must disconnect and reconnect the service drop, the entire process — from permit application to final inspection — typically spans three to five weeks. Reno Stars coordinates all utility bookings so homeowners do not manage this themselves.

Is a permit required for an electrical panel upgrade in Vancouver?

Yes. Any work that adds a new circuit or changes the panel rating requires an electrical permit from BC Safety Authority. The load calculation must be submitted with the permit application. Reno Stars handles this as part of every whole-home renovation that includes electrical work.

Will my power be off during the panel upgrade?

Yes, typically for one full day while BC Hydro disconnects the service drop and the new panel is installed. Reno Stars coordinates with BC Hydro to schedule this on a day that minimises disruption. The homeowner is without power for the duration of the utility work, usually 4–8 hours.

What is the difference between 100-amp and 200-amp service?

A 100-amp panel can handle most single-family homes with a standard appliance load. A 200-amp panel is required when a home has (or will have) multiple high-draw appliances running simultaneously — such as two EV chargers, a heat pump HVAC system, and an induction range. Reno Stars recommends 200-amp service for any whole-home renovation that includes three or more electric appliances.
contentZh:
温哥华基尔塞达尔、邓巴和莱利公园社区的大多数房屋在建造时都配备了60安培的配电服务。60安培的配电箱无法安全地为同时运行的现代厨房电器——电磁炉、热泵热水器和电动汽车充电器——供电。Reno Stars在全屋装修和重大线路改造期间将这些配电箱升级至100或200安培。

温哥华房屋何时需要升级配电箱？

当现有服务无法处理预期负载时，就需要升级配电箱。加拿大电气规范要求在任何新增大型电器之前进行负载计算。如果现有电路之和加上新电磁炉（通常为40至60安培）超过配电箱额定值，则需要进行升级，装修才能通过检查。

Reno Stars在每个全屋装修估算中都包含负载计算。这不是可选的——卑诗省安全管理局在温哥华发放电气许可证之前要求提供此计算。

升级工作包括哪些内容？

工作遵循可预测的顺序。首先，当地公用事业公司（温哥华的BC Hydro）断开服务线路。拆除旧配电箱，安装新的100安培或200安培断路器面板。新分支电路通向每个房间，通常使用14 AWG电线用于照明，12 AWG用于一般插座。厨房电器需要专用的40至60安培240伏电路。

温哥华的许可证费用约为200至300加元，BC Hydro可能收取300至600加元的服务线路升级费用（取决于与变压器的距离）。100安培配电箱升级的材料成本通常为1,500至3,000加元，人工费用另加1,000至2,500加元，具体取决于布线的年限。

正在规划厨房、浴室、全屋或商业装修？联系Reno Stars获取免费、无义务的报价。

温哥华装修中配电箱升级的时间表

简单的100安培配电箱更换需要一至两天。如果装修同时涉及整屋重新布线——如全屋装修——电气阶段通常跨越两到三周。时间表分解如下：

  • 负载计算和许可证申请：3至7个工作日（温哥华检查机构）
  • BC Hydro服务断开和重新连接：协调预订，通常提前1至2周
  • 配电箱更换和初始电路：1至2天
  • 最终电路整理和检查：1天

Reno Stars直接与BC Hydro和温哥华检查机构协调，因此业主无需管理任何这些预订。这避免了最常见的延误：业主等待他们不知道需要安排的公用事业预约。

影响温哥华装修的2025年加拿大电气规范变更

2025年加拿大电气规范（CEC）对住宅卧室和厨房的电弧故障断路器（AFCI）提出了更严格的要求，并扩大了新建配电箱安装中浪涌保护的要求。这些变更适用于2025年1月1日之后申请的所有许可证。Reno Stars对新配电箱安装的规格包括组合AFCI/断路器面板作为标准配置，这满足了2025年CEC要求，无需单独的浪涌保护装置。

带有保险丝式面板的房屋（1965年前温哥华房屋中发现的圆形玻璃保险丝）不符合2025年规范的祖父条款。任何触发电气许可证的装修都必须将面板升级至当前规范，包括整个过程中的电弧故障保护。

温哥华配电箱升级需要多少钱？

根据Reno Stars 2025年完成的温哥华地区装修项目记录，在全屋装修期间升级100安培配电箱的总费用通常在2,500至5,500加元之间（材料、人工、许可证和公用事业协调）。为多个电动汽车充电器或热泵HVAC系统供电的200安培升级，费用在4,000至8,000加元之间。

这些数字与BC Hydro公布的Metro Vancouver地区服务升级估算一致。确切的成本取决于与BC Hydro变压器的距离，以及是否可以重复使用现有的导管线路。

正在规划厨房、浴室、全屋或商业装修？联系Reno Stars获取免费、无义务的报价。

常见问题

温哥华厨房装修需要升级60安培配电箱吗？

如果添加电磁炉、双烤箱或即热式电热水器，大多数情况下是的。温哥华建筑规范要求在这些电器连接之前进行负载计算。如果计算表明现有60安培服务不足，则需要升级至至少100安培，装修才能通过检查。

全屋装修期间配电箱升级需要多长时间？

100安培配电箱更换的物理安装需要一至两天。由于BC Hydro必须断开和重新连接服务线路，整个过程——从许可证申请到最终检查——通常跨越三到五周。Reno Stars协调所有公用事业预订，因此业主不必自己管理。

温哥华配电箱升级需要许可证吗？

是的。任何添加新电路或更改配电箱额定值的工程都需要BC Safety Authority的电气许可证。负载计算必须与许可证申请一起提交。Reno Stars将其作为每个包含电气工程的全屋装修的一部分来处理。

配电箱升级期间电源会关闭吗？

是的，通常整整一天，BC Hydro断开服务线路并安装新配电箱。Reno Stars与BC Hydro协调，在最大程度减少干扰的一天安排此工作。业主在公用事业工作期间断电，通常持续4至8小时。

100安培和200安培服务有什么区别？

100安培配电箱可以处理带有标准电器负载的大多数单户住宅。当房屋同时拥有（或将拥有）多个高功耗电器时，需要200安培配电箱——例如两个电动汽车充电器、热泵HVAC系统和电磁炉。Reno Stars建议在任何包含三个或更多电器全屋装修中选择200安培服务。
